units.text: INT. SCRIVENER'S SHOP - FLORENCE - 1503 - DAY
A cramped room lined with ledgers and inkpots.
A high slanted desk by the window.
Sunlight cuts a gold bar across the floorboards.
Dust motes turn.
A MAN in a stained smock bends over a vellum sheet, quill scratching.
He is thin, quick, and does not look up when the bell above the door jingles.
A woman enters.
Dark cloak, veil.
She closes the door softly and stands with her hands clasped.
I was told you write letters for those who cannot.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: I write for those who will not.
units.name: MAN

units.text: That is a distinction.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: It is the whole of my profession.
units.name: MAN

units.text: He lifts his head.
Studies her.
She does not raise the veil.
Your name?
units.name: MAN

units.text: Not yet.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: Then I cannot write you a letter.
units.name: MAN

units.text: A letter does not need my name. Only his.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: Whose?
units.name: MAN

units.text: She crosses to the desk and lays a ring on the vellum.
A small gold band, set with a dark stone.
He picks it up.
Turns it in the light.
His quill stops.
Messer Giuliano.
units.name: MAN

units.text: You know him.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: Everyone knows him.
units.name: MAN

units.text: She lifts her veil at last.
A young face, pale, composed.
Her eyes do not leave his.
Then you know why I need a letter that will arrive after I am gone.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: The scrivener sets down the ring.
Dips his quill.
Begins to write.
Dictate, Madonna. I am listening.
units.name: SCRIVENER

units.text: Outside, a church bell tolls the hour.
She draws a breath, and begins.
